title: Flat scalar restriction respects the normalized direct-image/strict-limit comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_V$ be small sites and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_V)$ a geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. For $W=U,V$, let $a_W:R_W\to S_W$ be morphisms of sheaves of commutative rings with $S_W$ flat over $R_W$, meaning that $S_W\otimes_{R_W}-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Specify ring isomorphisms $u^{-1}R_V\simeq R_U$, $u^{-1}S_V\simeq S_U$ compatible with $a_U,a_V$. Assume countable products in the four module-sheaf categories are exact. All module and derived categories are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
For $Z=R,S$, let $F_Z=u_{*,Z}$ and $F_Z^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ be its termwise functor on strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Write $L_{W,Z}$ for total right derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Let $r_W$ denote scalar restriction, including its termwise tower and derived functors [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the canonical comparisons $d:r_VRF_S\simeq RF_Rr_U$ and $d^{\operatorname{Tow}}:r_VRF_S^{\operatorname{Tow}}\simeq RF_R^{\operatorname{Tow}}r_U$, normalized by the underived identity on K-injective complexes as in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction]. Use the resolution-normalized comparisons $\lambda_{r_W}:r_WL_{W,S}\simeq L_{W,R}r_W$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Let $c^Z_M:RF_ZL_{U,Z}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{V,Z}RF_Z^{\operatorname{Tow}}M$ be precisely the natural comparison induced by $F_Z\lim=\lim F_Z^{\operatorname{Tow}}$, computed by K-injective tower resolutions [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(S_U))$ the following equality holds:
$$L_{V,R}(d^{\operatorname{Tow}}_M)\circ\lambda_{r_V,RF_S^{\operatorname{Tow}}M}\circ r_V(c^S_M)=c^R_{r_UM}\circ RF_R(\lambda_{r_U,M})\circ d_{L_{U,S}M}.$$
It is natural in actual derived strict-tower morphisms. In particular, under these specified endpoint identifications the scalar restriction of $c^S$ is $c^R$, rather than merely an isomorphism with the same endpoints. For a K-injective $S_U$-tower complex $I$, the comparison is computed using that same complex and its K-injective restriction $r_UI$; the maps $d,d^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ and the scalar/limit comparisons on this model are induced by the underived scalar/direct-image/limit identities. No boundedness, completeness, finite-coefficient or etale-origin hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), common K-injective tower model; compatibility with flat scalar restriction in old item Step 8.

proof.text: Put $J_0=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its diagram sites are small, and their module categories are exactly the strict tower categories, by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on these sites. Thus we may compute at a K-injective $S_U$-tower complex $I$, and choose a quasi-isomorphism $j:F_S^{\operatorname{Tow}}I\to J$ with $J$ K-injective over $S_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction], applied both to $J_0$ and to the terminal category, restriction is exact and preserves K-injectives. In particular $r_UI$ and $r_VJ$ are K-injective tower complexes, and $r_Vj$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The hypotheses of that lemma hold: both coefficient maps are flat, the two ring identifications commute with them, and both indexing categories are small.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), tower ringed site; injectives.tex Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck), applied through the cited diagram-site equivalence.

proof.text: For each of the four module categories, the constant-tower functor $\Delta$ is additive and exact: its kernels and cokernels are the constant towers of the original kernels and cokernels, since these are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The defining universal property of inverse limit gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta B,T)=\operatorname{Hom}(B,\lim T)$, naturally in both variables. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to $\Delta\dashv\lim$. Consequently $\lim_{U,S}I$, $\lim_{U,R}r_UI$, $\lim_{V,S}J$ and $\lim_{V,R}r_VJ$ are K-injective module complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], these ordinary limits compute the corresponding total derived limits. This argument uses exactness of $\Delta$, not exactness of inverse limit.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), inverse limit as direct image; derived.tex Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives).

proof.text: Write $\alpha_T:r_VF_ST\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Rr_UT$ for the underived scalar/direct-image identification specified by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction], also levelwise on towers. Write $\beta_{W,T}:r_W\lim_{W,S}T\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim_{W,R}r_WT$. This is the identity on the underlying sheaf of compatible families: restriction changes only scalar action [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and the action on a limit is componentwise. It is therefore an isomorphism, natural in $T$, satisfying $\mathrm{pr}_n\beta_{W,T}=r_W(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. The identical argument for unrestricted families proves that $r_W$ preserves countable products with the canonical projection comparison. Finally let $e^Z_T:F_Z\lim_{U,Z}T\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim_{V,Z}F_Z^{\operatorname{Tow}}T$ be the ordinary identity used to define [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]; its defining equation is $\mathrm{pr}_ne^Z_T=F_Z(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. All these are chain maps when applied degreewise, since their naturality commutes with differentials.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), commutative tower-topos square; ordinary identities and their projection equations.

proof.text:
For every strict tower complex $T$ the ordinary comparisons satisfy
$$\lim_{V,R}(\alpha_T)\,\beta_{V,F_S^{\operatorname{Tow}}T}\,r_V(e^S_T)=e^R_{r_UT}\,F_R(\beta_{U,T})\,\alpha_{\lim_{U,S}T}.$$
Indeed, after composing either side with the $n$-th limit projection, the left side is $\alpha_{T_n}\,r_VF_S(\mathrm{pr}_n)$ and the right side is $F_R(r_U\mathrm{pr}_n)\,\alpha_{\lim T}$. These agree by naturality of $\alpha$; the limit projections determine a map uniquely. This proves the identity degreewise and hence as chain maps. Naturality of $\beta$ also gives
$$\beta_{V,J}\,r_V(\lim_{V,S}j)=\lim_{V,R}(r_Vj)\,\beta_{V,F_S^{\operatorname{Tow}}I}.$$
Both equations are universal-property calculations with the maps defined in Step 3; no uniqueness of maps of distinguished triangles is used.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), ordinary commutative square; explicit limit-projection calculation refining that square.

proof.text: Use $I,j,J$ from Step 1. Set $j_R=(r_Vj)\alpha_I^{-1}:F_R^{\operatorname{Tow}}r_UI\to r_VJ$. This is a K-injective resolution, since $r_Vj$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $r_VJ$ is K-injective. By [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-acyclic], both $\lim_{V,S}j$ and $\lim_{V,R}j_R$ are quasi-isomorphisms (apply it respectively to $I$ and $r_UI$). With the models in Step 2, the normalization of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] thus represents $c^S_{QI}$ by $Q(\lim j)Q(e^S_I)$ and $c^R_{Qr_UI}$ by $Q(\lim j_R)Q(e^R_{r_UI})$. Here $Q$ denotes localization in each relevant category. These are the prescribed common-direct-image comparisons: first use the ordinary composite identity $e$, then the target resolution. Since $\lim I$ is K-injective, the specified $d_{L_{U,S}QI}$ is represented by $Q(\alpha_{\lim I})$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction]. The same lemma represents $d^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{QI}$ by $Q(\alpha_I)$. Its derived limit is the identity on the common target model $\lim r_VJ$, because $j_R\alpha_I=r_Vj$.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), first proof and resolution normalization; the cited acyclicity statement justifies using the common target resolutions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] with $F=r_U$ and with $F=r_V$. Exactness was supplied in Step 1, the canonical product comparison is invertible by Step 3, and the four exact-countable-product hypotheses are precisely those assumed in the item. Its resolution-normalization clause allows the identity target resolutions $r_UI\to r_UI$ and $r_VJ\to r_VJ$, since these complexes are K-injective. Therefore $\lambda_{r_U,QI}$ is represented by $Q(\beta_{U,I})$, and $\lambda_{r_V,QJ}$ by $Q(\beta_{V,J})$. Both ends of $\beta_{U,I}$ are K-injective by Step 2 and flat restriction, so $RF_R(\lambda_{r_U,QI})$ is represented by $Q(F_R\beta_{U,I})$. Thus all five endpoint comparisons in the requested equality have their specified normalizations on these models.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), resolution construction; resolution-normalized scalar comparison as stated in lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit.

proof.text:
After the identifications of Steps 5 and 6, the left side of the requested equality is represented by
$$\beta_{V,J}\,r_V(\lim j)\,r_V(e^S_I).$$
The right side is represented by
$$\lim(j_R)\,e^R_{r_UI}\,F_R(\beta_{U,I})\,\alpha_{\lim I}.$$
The second equation of Step 4 rewrites the first expression as $\lim(r_Vj)\,\beta_{V,F_S^{\operatorname{Tow}}I}\,r_V(e^S_I)$. Substitute $\lim(r_Vj)=\lim(j_R)\lim(\alpha_I)$, which follows from the definition of $j_R$. The first equation of Step 4 then turns this into the second expression. Localizing this equality of chain maps proves exactly the displayed equality for $M=QI$, including its direction and all endpoint identifications.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), ordinary square refined by the two explicit identities in Step 4.

proof.text: Every derived strict-tower object has a K-injective representative by Step 1. For two such representatives, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] says that every actual derived morphism between them is represented by a chain map, uniquely up to homotopy. The maps $\alpha,\beta,e$ and the projection calculation of Step 4 are natural for such chain maps. Target resolutions may be chosen functorially by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the diagram sites. Additive functors preserve chain homotopies (apply the functor to $f-g=dh+hd$), so the calculation respects homotopies; a change of K-injective representative is a homotopy equivalence by the same Hom lemma. The resolution independence and naturality of $c$ and $\lambda$ are part of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] and [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Hence Step 7 proves the equality as a natural identity on the derived category of strict towers, not just on its evaluated inverse sequences. The source tower model is exactly $I$ and $r_UI$ throughout. Nothing in this argument requires boundedness or any of the additional coefficient or origin conditions excluded by the statement.
